title: Flamengo Beats Remo, Takes Lead with Record Attendance in Belém
seoTitle: Flamengo Defeats Remo, Becomes Leader with Record Crowd
subtitle: Marcelo Rangel's stunning save and a crowd of 51,000 fans mark the table-changing match
excerpt: Flamengo takes Brasileirão lead with a 1-0 win over Remo. The Mangueirão stadium saw record attendance and generated over six million reais in revenue.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: GE, O Dia, Folha de S.Paulo
contentHtml:
Flamengo defeated Remo 1-0 at the Mangueirão stadium in Belém, taking the lead in the Campeonato Brasileiro. The match was also marked by record attendance and an extraordinary save by Remo's goalkeeper.

Marcelo Rangel's Save Impresses

Marcelo Rangel, Remo's goalkeeper, made what is considered the best save of the Brasileirão so far. In the 10th minute of the second half, he denied Pedro's goal, who crossed the ball from the left, by stretching out his left arm and pushing the ball for a corner kick. After the match, Rangel joked with Pedro, saying, "It wasn't me, it was Jesus through me." Despite the save, Remo was eventually defeated by Samuel Lino minutes later.

Record Attendance and Historic Revenue

The Mangueirão welcomed 51,567 fans, the highest number of spectators at the stadium in 2026. The gross revenue from the match reached R$ 6.213 million, approximately 63% more than Remo's previous highest earnings, recorded against Palmeiras (R$ 3.814 million).

Flamengo Takes the Lead

With the victory, Flamengo reached 54 points, surpassing Palmeiras and becoming the new leader of the tournament. The club now relies solely on its own strength to pursue the title, with 12 rounds still to play.

Remo Remains in Relegation Zone

Remo remains in second-to-last position with 23 points and has been winless for six consecutive rounds. Goalkeeper Marcelo Rangel admitted he would trade his individual save for a victory, but emphasized the team's fight and their goal of staying in the top flight.

Upcoming Challenges

Remo returns to the field on Monday, the 14th, against Bahia at Fonte Nova, seeking to break their streak of negative results. Flamengo, meanwhile, remains strong in the fight for the Libertadores, with a direct confrontation against Athletico scheduled for November 22.

With information from GE, O Dia, Folha de S.Paulo.
